replication.target_description: Named Study 4 is a between-subject hypothetical college-decision scenario, with short-term, long-term and temporal-association tests; supplied personal-life description and unspecified horizon do not uniquely match.

notes: Identity assessment: substantive primary research-report parse with Methods, Results, Discussion, tables and references, rather than an abstract or preregistration. Repeated running title matches the supplied title through "With..."; journal is Collabra: Psychology. First-person replication of Gilovich and Medvec (1994), Studies 1a, 3, 4 and 5, with responsibility extensions, matches the neutral reference. No intact front matter/byline/DOI is present; Yeung and Feldman authorship, year and DOI 10.1525/collabra.37122 cannot be independently confirmed from document metadata. Substantively consistent source identity with bibliographic limitations; positives require independent parent review. No PDF supplied, so no rendering possible. Unassigned sides/fields are placeholders only. Study 4 identifier conflicts with personal-life description (Study 1a concerns general lifelong personal regret). Within Study 4, no horizon or association test is specified. Candidate participant Ns 247, 248 and 495 are explicit test-specific Ns, not a common sample to promote. No candidate chosen by values, row order or page number alone; no N sum. Study 4 candidates: χ2 (1, N = 247) = 14.09, p < .001 ... χ2 (1, N = 248) = 2.73, p = .099 ... χ2 (1, N = 495) = 14.68, p < .001. Alternative personal-life Study 1a: χ2 (1, N = 535) = 34.07, p < .001. Narrative evidence: We successfully replicated and found support for the original findings in Studies 1, 3, and 4 (short-term regret and temporal effect) with smaller effect sizes. For our replication of Study 4's long-term regret, the CIs of the replication did not cover the original effect size, and we failed to find support for the effect (which was the case in both the original and the replication). Recruitment 1017, overall post-exclusion sample 988 and 29 exclusions are not target-test N; detailed exclusion criteria are only in the unprovided supplementary. Study 4 Results percentages differ from Table 5; no reconstruction attempted.
